sense: an aim, a goal, a right

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, deponent, with the accusative
evidence: Hor. Ep. 1.1.72: nec sequar aut fugiam, quae dīligit ipse vel ōdit (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Mur. 55: ōtium ac tranquillitātem vītae (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The everyday verb “follow” (see follow), which with an aim or a good as its object is “seek, strive for” (Lewis & Short).

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, deponent, with the accusative
evidence: Cic. Off. 3.101: quis est, quī ūtilia nōn studiōsissimē persequātur? (Lewis & Short)
Ter. Ad. 2.1.9: ego meum jūs persequar (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Follow through to the end: an aim, an advantage, a right at law. Literally “chase” (see chase); also “go through, relate in full” (Lewis & Short).

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, with the accusative
terms.comment: Aim at, seek to obtain; also “ask for”, “make for (a place)” and “stand for (office)” (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: be devoted to, pursue (a study, an art)
terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation, with the dative
terms.comment: Give oneself to a pursuit; its general sense is “be eager for, care about”, and only later chiefly “study” (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: quis est, quī ūtilia nōn studiōsissimē persequātur?
phrases.english: who is there who does not pursue what is useful with the greatest zeal?

phrases.latin: nec sequar aut fugiam, quae dīligit ipse vel ōdit
phrases.english: and I shan’t pursue or shun what he himself loves or hates
